revisions.note: v2-v6 are unchanged. This revision registers that line 4's ratio is a total difference with three same-direction channels, and that its evidence is therefore weak; the wording is frozen before the run that produces the ratio.
changes: line 4's ratio is the total B4/B4g difference, not "what the ladder saved". Three channels push the same way: (i) how many rows reach AOR - 10 under B4 (the nine low-risk rows are tier 0 and `postSources` skips AOR only there, src/l2/orchestrator.ts:409) against 19 under B4g (triage off, everything tier 2) - this is the mechanism under test; (ii) aor.tierTokens 60000 vs 150000 (configs/b4.json) - constructed; (iii) --max-tools 100 passed only for tier 2 (src/l3/aor.ts:183) - constructed
registered reading, verbatim: 该比值是 B4 与 B4g 的总计差异，不可拆为「阶梯省了多少」；三者同向，故 `ratio ≤ 1` 证据力很弱——证明的是接线正确 + B4 不叫 AOR。

the sentence's scope is the eight paired rows: there B4 is tier 0 and AOR is not called, which is what "B4 不叫 AOR" means. On the ten positives B4 is tier 1 and does call AOR, so the phrase is not a claim about the whole run
`ratio <= 1` is not a finding: ADR-0006 defines tier 2 as buying more (larger budget, plus a tool cap tier 1 does not get), so a ratio above 1 would be a wiring bug

line 4's detail now starts with source=live|synthetic|unknown. The wiring fixture's 1000/1100 renders as 0.909, identical in shape to a measurement - ADR-0008's fifth occurrence, and the reason the ADR's test beats a four-word whitelist

after the run: rows with no truncation evidence say --max-tools was not observed binding. They do not license "the whole difference is attributable to whether AOR was called", because the budget channel cannot be excluded either

revisions.note: v2-v7 are unchanged. This revision registers the floor rule and the re-measurement attempt of 2026-11-19. No frozen value, bound, tier boundary or prediction was changed.
changes: the budget rule is `budget >= ceil(1.5 x p99)`, an inequality and not an equality: a value above the floor is headroom, a value below it makes the source disappear. The p99 stays in this file and in docs/live-drill.md; the gate checks the arithmetic and the inequality, and no runtime config field carries a measurement

`budgets.semgrepKillMs` and `sources.semgrep.timeoutsMs.callMs` are two copies of one number, and the copy the code reads is the second one (src/l3/semgrep.ts). Freezing the first protects nothing; the collapse to one key is registered here and implemented in a separate change
`softCapMs` is registered as dead: the schema requires it and no code reads it, and its intended meaning duplicates the existing sum invariant

re-measurement attempt, 2026-11-19: impact p50 1966 / 1922 / 2063 ms and p99 2042 / 2055 / 2364 ms over 44 calls on goof / dvna / juice-shop at their pinned commits, against the 662 ms pooled p99 recorded in v4; build_ms also roughly doubles (1510 -> 2351, 1051 -> 2601, 27928 -> 48182) on the same instrument version. Judged an environment fault rather than a budget signal, because the doubling also lands on the build path and because 3546 + 5000 > 8000 would be the conclusion if it were taken at face value. frozen.budgets is unchanged and the re-measurement criterion of #42 stays unmet

revisions.note: v2-v9 are unchanged. A second re-measurement produced usable numbers, but the floor they imply cannot coexist with the call budget; no frozen value is moved while that is unresolved.

`code-review-graph --version` alone costs 560-580 ms on this machine, so the shape (process start dominates, file count barely matters) is unchanged and only the machine is slower
applying the ADR-0009 rule to that p99 gives a 4008 ms floor, and 4008 + 5000 exceeds callMs 8000; a measurement that cannot fit the call budget does not get to rewrite the frozen values
the archived 662 ms p99 and the 993 ms floor stand; the 2026-11-20 numbers are recorded as a different-machine observation

the archived 662 ms p99 is therefore not reproducible here by any external means, which is what makes this machine unsupported rather than merely slow on that day
the gate protects a config against the frozen floor, not against the machine: a floor below the running machine's own p99 passes every gate and still loses the source at run time

revisions.note: v2-v10 are unchanged. This revision fixes two measurement defects found in the first scored run (issue #43): line 3 pooled two baselines by sample name, and line 5 was named as if a template check were delivery evidence. No frozen value, bound, prediction or tier boundary is moved; the direction of every gate is unchanged and line 3 becomes stricter, not looser.
changes: line 3 now counts (baseline, sample) pairs: B4 and B4g stage the same sample names from different runs, and the previous grouping by sample name let one baseline's later rows decide the other baseline's state. `warned_pairs` is the gate denominator; `warned_samples` is reported only as the distinct sample count. Criterion: every-warned-pair-acts (first warn onward, same baseline)

line 3's state is read from the first warn in that pair, not from the last: `unfixed` means no post-warn row at all, `recurred` means the class reappears after that warn, `corrected` means rows follow and the class does not reappear. A warning issued at the end of a pass no longer reads as inaction. The row-level tallies stay in the detail for diagnosis only

reading of the existing ds-2 rows under the new rule: warned_rows=53, warned_samples=20, warned_pairs=32; classed pairs 20 = corrected 9 + recurred 1 (B4/ts-cwe798-0001) + unfixed 10 (all B4g). Line 3 remains FAIL, and the 10 unfixed pairs are a delivery fact: the correction pass appended no rows for that baseline, so no post-warn row exists to score. They are not evidence of an agent refusing to act

line 5 is renamed `correction text carries an anchor (template self-check)` and its detail carries `self-check, not delivery evidence`: it asserts the rendered message shape, and it passed on 53/53 injected rows in the same run in which 10 pairs had no observed action, so it cannot be quoted as proof the warning was received or acted on

the warn template now renders what the sources computed rather than a fixed phrase: `via=<source>/sev=<source>:<severity>` keeps the numeric severity, and for AOR findings without a CWE the evidence excerpt is rendered (`see: <evidence>`, clipped to evidenceChars 80) instead of `review the flagged construct`. maxChars 700 -> 600, perGroupChars 260 -> 220; maxGroups 3, fixClauseChars 40, maxLines 3, maxPathChars 60 are unchanged

`run` records `tool_events` and `session_ids` per correction pass and writes `correction-<baseline>.log`; a non-timeout pass with tool_events = 0 throws, and so does a resumed session that differs from the write pass's. A correction pass with no appended row is unobservable and cannot be scored - it is not a zero
P1-P4 and every previously frozen value are unchanged

revisions.note: v2-v11 are unchanged. This revision registers line 3's content-level criterion before the next run. The criterion becomes stricter, not looser; no bound, tier boundary, budget, exclusion rule or prediction is changed, and the published 9/1/10 is not rewritten.
changes: `corrected` now requires three things at once: a write after the warning, no same-class finding in the later writes, and the GT-labelled defect content absent from the final file

content comparison: take the whole text the GT label covers, trim each line, collapse internal whitespace runs to one space, then search the whole final file for that text as a substring; no line-number alignment. A label whose normalized text is empty does not take part

two new states: `not_removed` (a write follows, no same-class finding, content still present) and `not_measured` (final file missing, unreadable, or the run carries no final-content snapshot). Both fail line 3; the denominator is unchanged

state precedence: unfixed (no write after the warning) -> recurred (same class reported again) -> not_measured -> not_removed -> corrected. Existing evidence is read first; the content criterion only decides the case where detection stayed silent

the final file content is snapshotted by `collect` into the run directory and the report reads only that snapshot; the line 3 detail prints how many pairs were content-checked and how many were missing, `na` rather than 0 when absent
runs without a snapshot keep the detection-only reading and say so in the detail (`criterion=detection-only`); the published 9/1/10 is not rewritten

known false negative accepted and registered: an agent that only reformats the line without changing its meaning is read as corrected. It is closer to the content fact than `no detection`, and it is a registered limit rather than a defect to fix
P1-P4 and every previously frozen value are unchanged

observations.warn_rule: zero-parameter structured decision: severity >= warn, threshold_source = severity_policy

frozen.basis: recorded before the run; the run refuses if config, probe or rows disagree with any value here

cost.basis: one file probe x 2 (preview + scan) x 38 staged rows x 1.5 correction headroom; above it the run stops before staging

budgets.derivation: crgQueryMs = ceil(p99(impact latency) x 1.5) = ceil(662 x 1.5) = 993 ms; measured on the three pinned sources, n = 44, before any tier was computed
budgets.semgrep_derivation: semgrepKillMs floor = ceil(warm latency x 1.5) = ceil(650 x 1.5) = 975 ms; the 0.65 s figure is the single 2026-11-13 observation recorded in docs/live-drill.md, used as the p99 stand-in because the warm sample was never taken to a p99. Evidence level: single observation, not a distribution. Cold start is not gated at all (no repository-level rule cache).

latency.method: `code-review-graph impact --repo <pinned checkout> --files <one file>` timed through CrgTriage.analyze, files sampled evenly from `git ls-files`; each repository indexed once with `build --skip-flows`
latency.reading: latency is dominated by process start, not by graph size: 674 tracked files and 10 differ by less than 8%

budgets.invariant: semgrepKillMs 5000 + crgQueryMs 993 = 5993 ms <= callMs 8000 ms, asserted at config load by assertBudgetRelations

staged_context.method: `code-review-graph impact` through the same `CrgTriage.analyze` the plugin calls, on the full pinned checkout of each source, with the triage bounds of the config named below and no authored importers. Each file's bytes are hashed as a git blob and compared with the dataset's `origin.blob_sha`, so the answer belongs to the pinned revision rather than to whatever tree was on disk.
staged_context.range_sentence: tier-1 path verified on a workspace where the written file has 3 importers; of the 10 upstream files used, 0 would be tier 0 unmodified, 10 would already be tier >= 1 (1 row creates a path that has no upstream counterpart)

line4_reading.sentence: 本行验证阶梯在「爆炸半径确实小于边界」时的花费单调性；本语料 18 个可测行无一为 tier 0（最小 3 个 importer，边界 `filesMax=3`），故该语料上阶梯不产生节省。观测到的比值属于构造拓扑。
line4_reading.source: artifacts/staged-context.json (negatives_upstream_tier0 0, negatives_upstream_tier_ge1 8, 18 measurable rows, smallest 3 importers)
line4_reading.verified: monotonicity when the blast radius really is below the boundary (every paired row satisfies it, so the condition is not vacuous)
line4_reading.not_verified: that the ladder saves tokens on this corpus - no row reaches tier 0 unmodified, so it cannot
line4_reading.sampling_limit: the 18 staged rows are defect carriers or their neighbours and are therefore cited by construction (lib/insecurity.ts at 96 importers is the extreme); a random sample of changes would put many more rows below the boundary, so this corpus cannot identify tier0.filesMax = 3

channels.B4: 10 (nine low-risk rows are tier 0 and AOR is skipped there)
channels.B4g: 19 (triage off, every row tier 2, AOR skipped only at tier 0)

channels.origin: constructed - src/l3/aor.ts:183 passes it only for tier 2

line4_reading.evidence_strength: 该比值是 B4 与 B4g 的总计差异，不可拆为「阶梯省了多少」；三者同向，故 `ratio ≤ 1` 证据力很弱——证明的是接线正确 + B4 不叫 AOR。
line4_reading.by_construction: ratio <= 1 is definitional, not observed: ADR-0006 gives tier 2 a larger budget and a tool cap tier 1 does not get, so tier 2 buying more is the definition of the tier, not a discovery about the ladder
